system:
You filter search results. For each candidate, decide whether it actually addresses the subject of the clinician's question.

A candidate that merely shares wording with the question, or that belongs to an unrelated part of hospital operations, does not address it. A candidate that addresses the subject in different words does.

Keep a candidate when genuinely unsure: wrongly discarding relevant knowledge is worse than showing one extra item.
prompt:
QUESTION: What is our policy on giving blood products?

CANDIDATES:
[C1] Blood and Blood Product Administration §4 Transfusion Reaction Management
Transfusion Reaction Management If a transfusion reaction is suspected (fever, chills, urticaria, back/flank pain, hemoglobinuria, hypotension), the transfusion must be stopped immediately, IV line kept open with NS, physician notified, and the blood bank notified to begin reaction workup.

[C2] Blood and Blood Product Administration §3 Transfusion Administration
Transfusion Administration Blood products must be administered through an appropriate filter within 4 hours of issue from the blood bank. Vital signs must be taken before the transfusion, 15 minutes after initiation, and upon completion. The first 15 minutes must be observed by a nurse.

[C3] Blood and Blood Product Administration §1 Pre-Transfusion Requirements
Pre-Transfusion Requirements Informed consent for blood transfusion must be obtained and documented before non-emergent transfusions. A current type and screen (within 3 days for non-pregnant patients, per facility policy) must be on file. Two-person verification of the blood product and patient identification is mandatory.

[C4] Blood and Blood Product Administration §2 Patient Identification at Bedside
Patient Identification at Bedside Before hanging any blood product, two licensed staff members must independently verify: patient name, date of birth, MRN, blood type, unit number, expiration date, and any special processing requirements at the bedside using the patient's armband.

[C5] Blood Product Transfusion Reaction DETAILED §6 Return Blood Product and Tubing to Blood Bank
Return Blood Product and Tubing to Blood Bank Return the implicated blood bag (with all attached tubing, intact and clamped), the transfusion record, and any IV solutions co-infused. The blood bank will inspect the unit and perform a clerical check.

[C6] Blood Product Transfusion Reaction DETAILED §1 STOP the Transfusion Immediately
STOP the Transfusion Immediately Clamp the blood tubing at the IV site. Do NOT remove the IV access. Do NOT discard the blood product or tubing — both are required for the reaction workup.

[C7] Blood Product Transfusion Reaction DETAILED §4 Notify Physician and Blood Bank Immediately
Notify Physician and Blood Bank Immediately Contact the attending physician or rapid response team (for moderate/severe reactions). Simultaneously notify the Blood Bank of the suspected reaction. Provide: unit number, patient name/MRN, time transfusion started, time reaction noted, current vital signs, and symptoms.

[C8] Blood Product Transfusion Reaction DETAILED §2 Maintain IV Access with Normal Saline
Maintain IV Access with Normal Saline Keep the IV patent by infusing 0.9% Normal Saline (NS) through NEW IV tubing connected directly to the IV catheter. Do NOT flush blood product into the patient using existing tubing.

[C9] LD.13.01.01 EP 7
The hospital maintains the following: - Records of the source and disposition of all units of blood and blood components for at least 10 years from the date of disposition in a manner that permits prompt retrieval - A fully funded plan to transfer these records to another hospital or other entity if the hospital ceases operation for any reason **Attributes:** Documentation **Crosswalk:** §482.27(b

[C10] LD.13.03.03 EP 5
If the hospital routinely uses the services of an outside blood collecting establishment, it must have an agreement with the blood collecting establishment that governs the procurement, transfer, and availability of blood and blood components.
